newsitem.title: USA: Late-season tropical storm in Caribbean kills two.
newsitem.headline: Late-season tropical storm in Caribbean kills two.

text.p: Tropical Storm Marco gained strength on Tuesday, leaving two dead in Nicaragua as it edged slowly through the Caribbean on a track that forecasters said could bring it to Jamaica and eastern Cuba later this week.

At 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT), Marco was near latitude 13.9 north and longitude 80 west, about 355 miles (570 km) southwest of Kingston, Jamaica, and moving eastward at six mph (10 kph), with a gradual turn toward the northeast forecast during the next 24 hours, the National Hurricane Centre said.

Nicaraguan civil defence authorities blamed at least two deaths on Marco after flooding that washed away homes in the Pacific coast and northern regions. They said one person had died in a traffic accident and another by drowning.
Maximum sustained winds had increased to near 60 mph (95 kph) and further strengthening was possible during the next 24 hours.

"There is a possibility that it could become a hurricane in about two or three days. Conditions are not ideally favourable for intensification but it's getting better," Lixion Avila, a specialist at the National Hurricane Centre, said.
Tropical storm force winds extended up to 105 miles (165 km) from Marco's centre. Forecasters warned of continuing heavy rain over parts of Central America for a day or two.

A tropical storm watch was in effect for Jamaica and forecasters said all of the western and central Caribbean region, particularly Jamaica, Cuba and the island of Hispaniola -- home to Haiti and the Dominican Republic -- should monitor the storm's progress.
"All the models are taking this tropical storm toward Jamaica and then toward eastern Cuba," Avila said.

Tropical storm watches indicate forecasters believe tropical storm conditions could threaten coastal areas within 36 hours. Tropical depressions become tropical storms when sustained winds top 39 mph (62 kph). A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when its maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph).
This year's Atlantic hurricane season officially ends on Nov. 30.
